Share on X Telegram ……Retains Only Mature Inclusivity Ranking Nigeria’s Inter-Bank Settlement System (NIBSS) Instant Payment (NIP) platform has retained its position as Africa’s only instant payment system to attain the highest maturity ranking for financial inclusion, standing out among 39 live payment systems assessed across the continent in the 2026 State of Inclusive Instant Payment Systems (SIIPS) in Africa Report.
The report, released by AfricaNenda, showed that while the number of live instant payment systems assessed across Africa had increased from 29 in 2022 to 39 in 2026, NIP remained the continent’s sole system in the Mature category, the highest of the four classifications used to measure inclusivity.
The report ranked instant payment systems based on their level of inclusivity, using four categories: Not Ranked, Basic, Progressed and Mature. Despite improvements recorded by other payment systems across Africa, NIP remained the only platform to attain the highest maturity classification.
Among the systems that recorded progress were Kenya’s PesaLink, Sierra Leone’s Salone Payment Switch and the Southern African Development Community’s (SADC) TCIB, which moved from the Not Ranked category to Basic.
The Pan-African Instant Payment and Settlement Infrastructure (PI-SPI) of the West African Economic and Monetary Union (WAEMU) also commenced operations as a progressed system.
NIBSS Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, Premier Oiwoh, attributed the platform’s continued classification to sustained investments in payment infrastructure and collaboration among stakeholders in Nigeria’s financial services industry.
“This recognition reaffirms Nigeria’s leadership in building an inclusive, interoperable, and trusted instant payments ecosystem. NIP’s Maturity status reflects years of sustained investment in infrastructure, innovation, and collaboration with the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), banks, fintechs, MFBs, PSSPs and other regulators to ensure that every Nigerian can transact instantly, safely, and affordably.”
He said the National Payment Stack (NPS), an upgraded payment infrastructure building on NIP, is expected to expand the benefits available to users.
The report identified key features underpinning NIP’s maturity classification, including the breadth of its functionality, affordability, dispute resolution mechanisms and participation of different payment service providers.
The platform also supports multiple transaction categories, including person-to-person (P2P), person-to-business (P2B), business-to-business (B2B) and government payments.
AfricaNenda’s annual SIIPS report assesses the development of inclusive instant payment systems across the continent, with a focus on their capacity to promote financial inclusion and support interoperable digital economies.
